battle.name: 1805年埃及革命
battle.brief: 中文維基戰爭列表將1805年埃及革命列為獨立衝突；這場變動發生於穆罕默德・阿里在埃及重建地方軍政權力、削弱舊有奧托曼控制之際。輪發槍（Wheellock pistol）自1500年列裝，是歐洲早期火器體系中的單兵手槍型號。

kit.name: 輪發槍
kit.history: 最早的後膛手槍。機械太貴，只給火槍隊的軍官與衛兵。

countries: 「1805年埃及革命」不是現代埃及史家通常使用的固定戰役名稱。若將它作為標題，最接近且可核實的史實，是法軍於1801年撤出埃及後，奧斯曼帝國試圖重建對埃及的直接軍權，並與仍掌握武裝家系的馬穆魯克貝伊交鋒。戰區以亞歷山卓亞、羅塞塔、尼羅河三角洲道路、開羅及開羅城堡為核心，後續補給與追擊則沿尼羅河谷向南延伸。交戰者並非兩個現代國家：一方是奧斯曼帝國、駐埃及省軍及阿爾巴尼亞軍團，另一方是數個各自擁有騎兵與步兵的馬穆魯克首領家系。英法在埃及的軍事活動屬於此前的權力背景，並不是1805年主要戰場上的交戰軍。
countriesEn: The phrase 1805 Egyptian revolution is not the standard fixed name of a battle or campaign in modern Egyptian historiography. Used as a title, it most closely refers to the Ottoman attempt to restore direct military authority after the French withdrawal in 1801, while several Mamluk beys still commanded armed households. The main operational area covered Alexandria, Rosetta, the roads of the Nile Delta, Cairo, and the Cairo Citadel, with supply and pursuit later extending south along the Nile Valley. The belligerents were not two modern nation-states. One side consisted of the Ottoman Empire, its Egyptian provincial garrison, and Albanian formations in Ottoman service; the other comprised separate Mamluk houses that fielded their own cavalry and infantry. British and French activity in Egypt formed the preceding strategic background, but neither was a principal field army in the 1805 fighting.
people: 核心人物是穆罕默德·阿里·帕夏，生於1769年，卒於1849年；1805年時他仍是奧斯曼政府麾下的阿爾巴尼亞軍團指揮官，尚未成為獨立統治者。伊斯坦堡的塞利姆三世中央政府及蘇丹授權他處理埃及軍務，埃及省軍、炮隊、工兵和後勤官員則構成奧斯曼方面的指揮鏈。馬穆魯克一方沒有單一總司令，而是由若干貝伊分別率領自己的頭巾家系、侍從、騎兵與步兵；前一代阿里貝伊已於1803年死亡，不可能是1805年戰場上的指揮者。關於穆罕默德·阿里的核心部隊，史料可以確定是數千人的阿爾巴尼亞作戰部隊，但常把省軍、援軍及臨時武裝混在一起，不能把三萬之類的概括數字直接當作實際作戰兵力。馬穆魯克各部的數量也會隨地域、附庸及投降與否而變動。
peopleEn: The central figure was Muhammad Ali Pasha, born in 1769 and deceased in 1849. In 1805 he was still a commander of Albanian formations in Ottoman service rather than an independent sovereign. Selim III and the Ottoman central government authorized him to conduct military affairs in Egypt, while the provincial garrison, artillery crews, engineers, and logistical officials formed the Ottoman command structure. The Mamluk side had no single commander-in-chief: several beys independently led their turbaned households, retainers, cavalry, and infantry. Ali Bey al-Kabir had died in 1803 and was not a commander in the 1805 fighting. The surviving evidence supports a core Albanian field force numbering in the thousands, but Ottoman provincial troops, reinforcements, and ad hoc armed men are often combined in later figures. A claim of thirty thousand should therefore not be treated as an exact combat strength. Mamluk participation also varied with location, allegiance, and subsequent submission.
kits: 1805年能夠確定的裝備類型包括奧斯曼省軍與阿爾巴尼亞部隊使用的燧發滑膛步槍、部分仍殘存的火繩步槍、插柄式刺刀、亞特干彎刀及較長的軍刀；馬穆魯克騎兵則可使用阿拉伯馬、高鞍、標槍、彎刀、燧發手槍、長身火槍、小圓盾，以及少量鎖子甲和頭盔。野戰炮通常為六磅或十二磅青銅滑膛炮，城堡則可能配置更重的舊式火炮；炮彈包括實心鐵彈、葡萄彈及配套火藥。步兵通常攜帶定量火藥和鉛彈，炮隊使用較大的火藥量與彈藥箱。作戰和運輸還需要馬匹、駱駝、驢騾、載重鞍具、_cart車，以及能沿尼羅河輸送人員、飼料與彈藥的各類 boats。這個時期尚未普遍使用後來常見的雷管擊發槍或後膛炮，因此不應把十九世紀中葉以後的裝備倒置到1805年的戰鬥中。
kitsEn: Historically secure equipment for 1805 includes flintlock muskets used by Ottoman provincial and Albanian troops, some surviving matchlock muskets, socket bayonets, yataghans, and longer military sabres. Mamluk cavalry could use Arabian horses, high saddles, lances, scimitars, flintlock pistols, long firearms, small round shields, and limited quantities of mail and helmets. Field artillery commonly consisted of six- or twelve-pounder bronze smoothbore guns, while older and heavier pieces remained in citadels. Ammunition included solid iron shot, grapeshot, and corresponding powder charges. Infantry carried measured quantities of powder and lead bullets, whereas artillery batteries required larger powder charges and dedicated ammunition boxes. Horses, camels, donkeys or mules, pack saddles, carts, and various Nile boats were required to move troops, fodder, and ammunition. Percussion ignition and breech-loading artillery had not yet become standard, so weapons characteristic of the middle and later nineteenth century should not be placed in the 1805 battlefield.
tactics: 作戰重心不是一次大型正面會戰，而是控制道路、渡口、尼羅河運輸線和城防，再迫使分散的馬穆魯克家系逐次表態。奧斯曼與阿爾巴尼亞步兵常以小隊沿灌溉渠、堤岸和建築物掩體前進，在數十至一百多步內利用燧發槍反覆射擊；距離被壓縮後，再以刺刀和軍刀守住陣線。炮隊會選擇堅硬地面佈置，以實心鐵彈打擊衝鋒或追擊中的騎兵，近距離則可使用葡萄彈。馬穆魯克騎兵避免長時間停留在密集火線下，而以快速襲擾、兩翼迂迴、假退及切斷道路等方式迫使敵方分兵；他們也會利用村落間狹窄道路與地形起伏，從侧面攻擊較長的步兵縱隊。穆罕默德·阿里通常讓步兵和炮隊固定主要陣地，再以騎兵追擊退回或脫離接觸的馬穆魯克武裝。這套方法顯示出控制補給與射擊陣地的重要性，但現有材料不足以重建每一次小規模衝突的完整隊形。
tacticsEn: The central operational problem was not a single massed field battle but the control of roads, crossings, Nile transport routes, and fortifications, followed by pressure on separate Mamluk households. Ottoman and Albanian infantry often advanced in small bodies along irrigation channels, levees, and buildings, delivering repeated flintlock volleys at ranges of several dozen to more than one hundred paces. When the distance contracted, they defended the line with bayonets and sabres. Artillery was positioned on firm ground, using solid shot against cavalry during charges or pursuits and grapeshot at close range. Mamluk riders generally avoided remaining under dense musket fire for long periods. They relied on rapid raids, flank movement, feigned withdrawals, and attacks against roads and extended columns, using narrow approaches and changes in elevation to strike infantry from the side. Muhammad Ali commonly anchored his position with infantry and guns, then sent cavalry after Mamluk groups that withdrew or broke contact. The evidence demonstrates the importance of communications and firing positions, although it does not permit a complete reconstruction of every minor action.
data: 1801年法軍完成撤離後，埃及重新落入奧斯曼政府的形式控制，但馬穆魯克武裝仍能離開自己的控制區活動。1804年，穆罕默德·阿里率領奧斯曼部隊參與對馬穆魯克勢力的軍事行動；到1805年初，他利用亞歷山卓亞、羅塞塔與三角洲道路組成的補給線向開羅方向推進。馬穆魯克分隊曾以騎兵遮斷道路、渡口及接近開羅的高地，奧斯曼軍則先以步兵建立據點，再把野戰炮運到能控制通行線的位置。現存材料顯示雙方進行過反覆的小規模接觸，而不是一場可以完整記錄雙方縱隊與傷亡的單日會戰。入春後，穆罕默德·阿里逐步占領開羅並控制城堡；1805年3月前後的中央任命，使他的角色由前線指揮官轉為奧斯曼中央承認的埃及總督。他以開羅為後勤和駐軍支點，沿通往上埃及的道路派出分遣隊，使部分貝伊率部投降或退往其他控制區，另一些武裝則繼續向南移動。進入1805年下半年，開羅、尼羅河三角洲及下埃及的主要交通線已較穩定地置於穆罕默德·阿里與奧斯曼省軍控制之下，但上埃及仍有馬穆魯克勢力，故這一年的行動只是鞏固過程的起點和重要階段，而不是馬穆魯克制度的彻底终结。把它稱為1805年金字塔戰役也很容易與1798年7月21日法軍戰役混淆，可靠年表並不支持把上述行動壓縮成金字塔旁的一場決戰。
dataEn: After the French evacuation was completed in 1801, Egypt returned to nominal Ottoman control, although Mamluk armed households could still operate beyond their immediate territories. In 1804 Muhammad Ali led Ottoman troops in operations against those armed groups. By early 1805 he was using the supply connections linking Alexandria, Rosetta, and the Delta roads while moving toward Cairo. Mamluk detachments attempted to interrupt roads, crossings, and high ground near the approaches to the capital. The Ottoman force established infantry positions first and then brought field artillery to locations commanding the routes. The surviving evidence points to repeated small engagements rather than a single action for which both lines and casualties can be completely reconstructed. By spring, Muhammad Ali had occupied Cairo and gained control of the Citadel. The central appointment around March 1805 recognized him as governor of Egypt rather than merely a field commander. Using Cairo as a garrison and logistical base, he sent columns along roads toward Upper Egypt. Some beys submitted or withdrew with their followers, while other armed groups moved farther south. During the second half of 1805, Cairo, the Nile Delta, and the principal routes of Lower Egypt were more securely held by Muhammad Ali and the Ottoman provincial forces, but Mamluk power remained in Upper Egypt. The year therefore marked an important stage of consolidation rather than the final destruction of the Mamluk military order. Calling these events a pyramid battle in 1805 also risks confusion with the French battle fought on July 21, 1798, and the reliable chronologies do not support reducing the campaign to one decisive battle beside the pyramids.
cause: 這場軍事行動的直接背景，是法國 invasion及其撤離打亂了奧斯曼省軍、馬穆魯克貝伊與地方武裝之間原有的權力平衡。馬穆魯克家系長期保有武裝、騎兵、部分土地收入和地方軍事網絡，形式上承認奧斯曼宗主权，卻不一定接受省總督對全部埃及軍隊的直接調度。1801年後奧斯曼中央希望重新派遣省軍、稅收官和炮隊進入開羅，以削弱馬穆魯克首領的獨立支配；穆罕默德·阿里的阿爾巴尼亞部隊則被選為執行這一任務的力量。對他而言，埃及總督職位同時提供了擴大個人軍事、財政與政治權力的機會。 因此，1805年的衝突本質上是奧斯曼中央集權、地方軍閥與軍事職業指揮官之間的權力競爭，而沒有全國性的政治綱領或統一革命軍能夠把這些力量整合起來。用革命一詞容易掩蓋它實際上的省政府接管、軍事集結與政權轉移性質。
causeEn: The immediate background was the disruption of the balance among Ottoman provincial forces, Mamluk beys, and local armed groups caused by the French invasion and subsequent evacuation. Mamluk households had long retained military organizations, cavalry, portions of land revenue, and regional networks. They formally acknowledged Ottoman suzerainty but did not uniformly accept direct orders from the provincial governor. After 1801, the Ottoman center sought to strengthen its authority by deploying provincial troops, fiscal officials, and artillery into Cairo, thereby reducing the independent control of the beys. Muhammad Ali's Albanian formations were selected to carry out this task. For him, the governorship also offered an opportunity to expand his own military, fiscal, and political power. The conflict of 1805 was therefore a struggle among Ottoman central authority, regional military households, and a professional field commander. It did not possess a nationwide program or unified revolutionary army capable of joining those forces under a common political cause. The word revolution consequently obscures the actual combination of provincial government, military mobilization, and transfer of coercive authority.
impact: 1805年最重要的結構性影響，是埃及的主要軍事力量開始由馬穆魯克貝伊的家系轉向奧斯曼省軍與穆罕默德·阿里的阿爾巴尼亞指揮系統。占據開羅、城堡和三角洲交通線後，阿里的部隊能從固定的後勤基地取得糧食、弹药和增援，而不斷在各個武裝集團之間選擇戰與降的時機。中央政府的任命也讓他取得徵募、財政與省級行政資源，這些資源後來成為建立相對獨立統治能力的基礎。尼羅河運輸、羅塞塔與亞歷山卓亞方向的供應，以及部署在道路和渡口的火炮，逐漸提高奧斯曼方面的戰略持續性。不過，馬穆魯克制度並未在1805年被一次清除；其家系仍保有土地、軍事傳統和上埃及的若干據點。此後數年的戰爭正源於這種未完成的轉換。阿里的勝利鞏固了開羅和下埃及，卻也顯示奧斯曼中央對埃及的直接控制，往往必須依靠具有自身政治目標的地方指揮官。
impactEn: The most important structural effect of 1805 was the beginning of a shift in Egypt's principal military power from the Mamluk beys' households toward the Ottoman provincial forces and Muhammad Ali's Albanian command system. After taking Cairo, the Citadel, and the Delta communications, Ali could draw food, ammunition, and reinforcements from fixed logistical bases and choose the moment to fight or accept the submission of individual armed groups. His central appointment also gave him authority over recruitment, finance, and provincial administration. Those resources later became the foundation of a more autonomous government. The Nile transport system, supply lines through Rosetta and Alexandria, and artillery placed at roads and crossings gradually increased the strategic endurance of the Ottoman side. The Mamluk order, however, was not abolished in a single stroke. Its households retained lands, military traditions, and positions in Upper Egypt, and fighting continued as this incomplete transformation developed. The immediate result was stronger control of Cairo and Lower Egypt, but it also showed that direct Ottoman authority in Egypt depended on local commanders whose political objectives increasingly exceeded those of the central government.
result: 以1805年12月為界，穆罕默德·阿里與奧斯曼埃及省軍已控制開羅、城堡、尼羅河三角洲和下埃及的主要補給路線；部分馬穆魯克貝伊率部投降或退往南部，其餘武裝仍能在上埃及活動。因此，若只衡量1805年的首都與交通線控制，結果是穆罕默德·阿里的軍事勝利；若以彻底消滅馬穆魯克軍事力量為標準，戰爭仍未結束。奧斯曼方面的實際進展來自炮兵掩護、步兵據點、騎兵追擊和對尼羅河交通的逐步控制，而不是一次決定全部局勢的會戰。現存史料無法可靠提供整場行動的死亡、被俘人數或損失火炮總量，因此不能列出精確傷亡數字。把1805年事件稱為革命，只能概括中央任命與軍事主導權轉移到穆罕默德·阿里手中的結果，不能表述為埃及全國武裝推翻舊政權。馬穆魯克影響的最終衰退發生在1810年代初，而1805年留下的核心成果，是開羅與下埃及已置於阿里及其部隊的實際控制之下。
resultEn: By the end of December 1805, Muhammad Ali and the Ottoman Egyptian forces controlled Cairo, the Citadel, the Nile Delta, and the principal supply routes of Lower Egypt. Several Mamluk beys had submitted or moved south with their followers, while other armed groups remained operational in Upper Egypt. Measured only by control of the capital and communications during 1805, the outcome was a military victory for Muhammad Ali. Measured by the complete destruction of Mamluk military power, the campaign remained unfinished. Ottoman progress resulted from artillery protection, fixed infantry positions, cavalry pursuit, and gradual control of Nile transport rather than from one battle that decided the entire conflict. Surviving sources do not support reliable totals for deaths, prisoners, or captured artillery, and no precise casualty figures should be supplied. Calling the events of 1805 a revolution can therefore describe only the transfer of central appointment and military leadership to Muhammad Ali; it cannot mean that a nationwide Egyptian armed force had overthrown the existing government. The final decline of Mamluk influence occurred in the early 1810s, whereas the immediate result of 1805 was that Cairo and Lower Egypt came under the effective control of Ali and his forces.
